I am a labor, health, and education economist and a lead research economist at the [Research and Innovation for Social and Economic Inclusion Lab](https://riseilab.org/) at Northwestern University. I am also a research affiliate at the [IZA Institute of Labor Economics](https://www.iza.org/person/34828/hussain-hadah) and Tulane University's [Murphy Institute](https://murphy.tulane.edu/).

## Discrimination and identity

I study how names, social attitudes, and public policy affect discrimination and ethnic self-identification. My published work examines Hispanic surnames in education and labor markets and the relationship between racial attitudes and Hispanic identity.

## Field experiments

My audit studies measure discrimination in mortgage lending and school admissions. The school-admissions project compares responses from traditional public, charter, and private schools to families who differ by race, ethnicity, disability, socioeconomic status, sexual orientation, or gender identity.

## Health, education, and labor

My other projects study peer effects in adolescent mental health, firearm waiting periods and suicide, immigration enforcement, disability services, and workforce-development policy. I use causal inference methods, field experiments, and administrative data to answer these questions.
